items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Al Hall was on bas$, and then I heard J.C. Heard in Detroit and brought him to New York, on drums -- J.C. was a swinging little drummer, he was a teenager when he joined my band

ctx.x: Give me the names of those guys.

Well, Al Hall was on bas$, and then I heard J.C. Heard in Detroit and brought him to New York, on drums -- J.C. was a swinging little drummer, he was a teenager when he joined my band, and he had never played in a big band in his life, but he was playing with Bill Johnson's band at the Cozy Corner in Detroit, I think it was.

items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: So with Teddy Wilson's big band, we opened at the Famous Door in May '39

ctx.x: Yes. Eddie Haywood, Teddy Wilson, they were the favorite pianists. Edgar Hayes. Clyde Hart. Billy Kyle hadn't come yet to New York.
Now, you were saying before when we were talking about the way the big band would stop and your band would take off, what was that.
